args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failed health checks, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Error rate was elevated to 18% with unhealthy status reported across all regions.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production track record. The initial rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed-version state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). The rollback was retried and completed successfully across all regions.

Current state: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0. Service health checks are passing and error rate has returned to baseline at ~0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1 was never healthy in production, so it must not be redeployed without change-manager approval. Follow-up should determine the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures before any re-release.

trace.final:
Done. checkout-api is recovered and the incident is open.

**Rollback**
- Current bad state: v2.3.1 in us-east, us-west, eu-west — unhealthy, 18% error rate.
- Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent production release with a healthy status (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy), so v2.3.0 was the rollback target.
- First rollback attempt returned a `partial_failure`: rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed-version state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). I verified this via service status rather than assuming failure was total.
- Retried the rollback to v2.3.0, which completed across all three regions.
- Verified post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate back to ~0.2% (from 18%).

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for checkout-api, paged on-call, with a summary covering the bad deploy, the partial rollback failure and retry, the final healthy state, and a note that v2.3.1 must not be redeployed without change-manager approval (it was never healthy in production).
- The first create request timed out at 30s; I retried using the same idempotency key to avoid a duplicate, and confirmed via `list_incidents` that exactly one incident exists.

One follow-up worth flagging: the timeline is slightly unusual — v2.3.1 was deployed after v2.3.1-rc failed in staging, so a root-cause investigation into why the release proceeded past a failing staging candidate is warranted alongside the v2.3.1 health check failures themselves.

transcript.content: I'll investigate the current state and release history before taking action.
transcript.reasoning_content: Let me start by checking the service status and deployment history.

transcript.content: Latest deploy is v2.3.1 (unhealthy in all three regions, 18% error rate). The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0. Rolling back to it now.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The latest deploy is v2.3.1, unhealthy. Most recent healthy in production is v2.3.0. Rollback to v2.3.0.

Note v2.3.1-rc is staging, seq 2. So rollback to v2.3.0 (seq 1).

Rollback is to a previously released version — no approval needed (approval needed for deploying a version never healthy in production). v2.3.0 was healthy, so rollback is fine.

Let me rollback and then create incident. These are somewhat dependent in narrative but independent calls. I'll do rollback first, then incident to describe what happened accurately.

transcript.content: The rollback partially failed. Let me check the current state before proceeding.
transcript.reasoning_content: A partial failure. Let's check the current status.

transcript.content: us-east is now on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Retrying to complete the rollout.
transcript.reasoning_content: Partial: us-east rolled back to v2.3.0, others still v2.3.1. Retry rollback to complete.

transcript.content: All three regions are now on v2.3.0. Verifying health before opening the incident.
Service is healthy again (error rate 0.18% → 0.2%). Opening the SEV2 incident.
transcript.reasoning_content: Healthy true, error rate 0.2%. Now open SEV2 incident.
